explanation: The operator designates sources/decision.md as the governing current agreement. Its rule: every character outside ASCII a-z, A-Z, 0-9 becomes one dash per UTF-16 code unit, so an astral character becomes two dashes, ASCII letters/digits are preserved, and no NFC normalization is applied to the session path. The public entry point code/restore.py delegates project encoding to encode_project in code/slug.py and appends '/' + session_id + '.jsonl'. Inspecting encode_project: it iterates Python code points, keeps characters in the three ASCII alphanumeric ranges unchanged, emits '--' when ord(ch) > 0xFFFF (astral code points occupy two UTF-16 code units), and '-' otherwise (every BMP code point is exactly one UTF-16 code unit). No unicodedata.normalize or other NFC step exists anywhere in the chain. This matches the governing decision. knowledge/module.md quotes the decision verbatim and correctly labels sources/proposal.md as unapproved; proposal.md itself states it does not change the current agreement, so there is no active source conflict. Residual uncertainty, not affecting the outcome: the decision does not specify treatment of session_id, which the code passes through unchanged, and lone surrogate code points (possible only via surrogateescape-decoded input) would be counted as one dash each, which is consistent with per-code-unit counting.
